gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: She ___ to the gym three times a week, mostly before work.
gaps.hint: three times a week shows a routine
gaps.explanation: Frequency expressions like 'three times a week' describe habits, which take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: They ___ so much since they started the new school.
gaps.hint: since they started with present result
gaps.explanation: Change measured from a past starting point to now takes the present perfect: have grown.

gaps.sentence: Don't worry about the dog — it ___ at strangers, but it never bites.
gaps.hint: typical behavior takes the present simple
gaps.explanation: Characteristic, repeated behavior takes the present simple: barks.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her grandmother every Sunday; it is a promise she never breaks.
gaps.hint: every Sunday marks repeated routine action
gaps.explanation: 'Every Sunday' signals a regularly repeated action, so the present simple is correct: visits.

gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.

gaps.sentence: When we were students, we ___ to live on instant noodles.
gaps.hint: a past habit with used to
gaps.explanation: 'Used to' plus the infinitive describes a past habit: used to live.

gaps.sentence: The train ___ faster than the bus, so we always take the train.
gaps.explanation: Timeless comparisons take the present simple: goes.
